test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7 Oct 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Select the correct statement.

options.text: A fiscal deficit is a shortfall in a government's income compared with its spending.
An annual statement of the government's fiscal revenue and fiscal expenditure known fiscal budget.
Capital budget is not a part of government budget.
The amount collected by the government in the form of interest, fees, and dividends is known as tax revenue receipt.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A fiscal deficit is a shortfall in a government's income compared with its spending.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A fiscal deficit occurs when a government's total expenditures exceed the revenue that it generates, excluding money from borrowings.
 
• It is an important measure of a government's financial health, indicating the extent to which government spending exceeds income.
 
• A high fiscal deficit can be a cause for concern as it implies that a government might be overspending or not generating sufficient revenue.
 
• Fiscal deficits can lead to increased government borrowing, which may result in higher public debt and interest payments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Budget:**

 
 
• An annual statement of the government's fiscal revenue and fiscal expenditure, showing the allocation and utilization of financial resources.
 
• It includes both the capital budget (long-term investments) and revenue budget (day-to-day expenditures).
 
 
 
• **Capital Budget:**
 
 
• Part of the government budget that includes spending on infrastructure, equipment, and other long-term investments.
 
• It is crucial for economic development and improving the productivity of the nation.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Receipts:**
 
 
• Income earned by the government from its regular operations, including taxes, interest, fees, and dividends.
 
• Tax revenue receipt specifically refers to income from taxes imposed on individuals and businesses.
 
 
 
• **Government Borrowing:**
 
 
• The process by which a government raises funds to cover its fiscal deficit.
 
• This borrowing can be from domestic sources (e.g., issuing government bonds) or international sources (e.g., loans from foreign governments or international organizations).
